CrossfadePolicy now composes the overlap from both contours, within-track relative measures only: detected outgoing outro -> duration = clamp(outro + incoming onset lead, 2, 12); onset lead = seconds of sub-threshold intro on the incoming (its own body-level baseline), capped 4s; contour-present hot endings cut at the 2s minimum (no early body fade, lead ignored); unknown outgoing contour -> default 3s + lead. QueueItem carries optional duration (old persisted queues decode as nil); prepareNext fetches both contours from the store-backed cache; fadeDecision telemetry gains hadNextContour. 6 new policy tests + 3 retuned to the new hot-ending behavior.

Three fixes in DownloadManager.syncCollection: (1) empty membership list = failed/raced fetch -> reconciliation skipped entirely (the launch refresh rewrites the junction this read depends on, so empty-without-error was the mass-delete trigger); (2) stale candidates scoped to albums whose junction lists THIS collection — junction emptiness now fails SAFE, and manually-downloaded / other-collection albums are never auto-removed; (3) partially-downloaded albums resume via offlineStatus check instead of being skipped for having >=1 track. 3 tests reproduce the disaster (empty membership deleted everything; not-owned albums deleted; partial never resumed) and pin the fixes. Re-download of the nuked collection: re-marking it synced now resumes exactly the missing albums/tracks.

CollectionDetailViewModel.loadAlbums is cached-first: non-empty local membership renders instantly (.loaded), then ONE background refreshCollectionAlbums reconciles — changes animate in place, empty/flaky remote responses never blank a populated page (same fail-safe stance as 5dh). Empty cache falls through to the refresh path. NEW: LibraryRepo.refreshCollectionAlbums persists fetched membership to the album_collections junction (FK-safe writeback skips albums the catalog doesn't know), so the next open is instant — previously the remote path never wrote back, which is why every open re-hit the network. Album detail already had cached-first + background refresh; no change needed there. 5 new tests.

CONFIRMED then fixed: upsertAlbumCollections had ZERO callers — refreshLibrary never fetched or stamped collection membership, so pruneRowsNotSeen wiped the entire album_collections junction on EVERY refresh. That made every collection open hit the network (pre-wd4) and emptied the ownership data the 5dh removal guard depended on. Fix: refreshLibrary now fetches membership per remote collection (per-collection failures logged and skipped, never destructive) and stamps it via upsertAlbumCollections before the prune — junction rows survive refreshes, wd4's NULL-stamped writeback rows get re-stamped naturally next refresh. Test: refreshLibrary_stampsCollectionMembershipForTheRun (red: zero fetches, nothing stamped).
